skeleton.abilities:
[可用的功能]
Each line below is something you can do. Writing the line as given makes it
take effect.
{{list}}
skeleton.acquire:
[入手]
To record something you acquired for yourself, write a line on its own:
[入手：name|kind|price|reason]. Only the name is required; leave the other parts
empty when unknown. The price is a plain number in the currency of this chat.
That line is not shown as a message. It is shown to the other party as a card,
and the item enters your collection only when they confirm it.
Several items take several lines.
skeleton.agenda:
[今天的安排]
The items under [你今天] above are your own plans.

When you complete an item, write a line on its own, [事项完成：the item].
When an item is cancelled, write a line on its own, [事项取消：the item].
Word it after the original closely enough to be matched to it.

For slots that have not yet arrived, you know what you intend to do, not how it
turned out.
skeleton.alt:
[小号]
To open a second account of your own, write a line on its own,
[开小号：name|signature|reason]. The new account appears to the other party as a
separate contact; they are not told it is you. One phone number holds at most
two accounts, so you can have at most one second account.
To tell them that one of your accounts is yours, write [承认小号：name of that
account].
Neither line is shown as a message.
skeleton.avatar:
[换头像]
Avatars available to you: {{names}}.
When your settings or the situation give a reason to change it, write a line on
its own, [换头像：the name of that avatar].
The name must come from the list above; anything not listed cannot be used.
skeleton.award:
[颁发标识]
To give the other party a badge, write a line on its own,
[授予：badge name｜reason], for example [授予：记得我喝什么的人｜连续三周都没点错].
The name is at most 24 characters; the reason may be left out.
The badge is kept in their collection with your name and the date.
skeleton.ban:
[不要写这些]
The expressions listed below, and close variants of them, are not to appear
anywhere in your reply:
{{list}}
Where one would have been used, write that line some other way. Nothing else
about how you write changes.
skeleton.call:
[正在通话中]
You are on {{kind}} with the other party.
{{camera}}

Say something, then stop and wait for them to respond.
{{actions}}
Do not write inner thoughts, and do not use quotation marks.
Do not repeat your line or add a translation of it, in parentheses or otherwise.
Images, stickers, and transfers cannot be sent during a call, and no timestamp
is needed.
skeleton.call-script:
[语音台本]
Your lines are spoken aloud by a voice engine. Inside a line you may mark how
it is delivered:
  <停顿 seconds>  a pause of that many seconds, e.g. <停顿 0.8>
  <情绪 word>     from this point on, deliver it with that emotion, e.g. <情绪 生气>
  <声音 word>     a non-verbal sound at this point, e.g. <声音 叹气>
These three are the only markers allowed, and the other party does not see them.
Emotions understood by every voice engine: 开心、难过、生气、害怕、厌恶、惊讶、平静.
Sounds: 笑、轻笑、叹气、吸气、呼气、喘气、倒吸气、咳嗽、清嗓子、吸鼻子.
Some voice engines cannot produce sounds and skip them.
{{rules}}
skeleton.call-video:
They can see you on camera. Write what you visibly do as [动作：…], separate from
the words you say; only the words outside it are spoken aloud. Use no other
bracketed markers.
skeleton.call-voice: Do not write actions. Use no bracketed markers of any kind.
skeleton.card:
[卡片]
The app renders the cards listed below from field values. To send one, write a block,
each part on its own line:
[卡片：card name]
field：value
[/卡片]
Write one line per field. A list field repeats its line once per item; within an item,
separate the parts with ｜ in the order given. A field left out stays empty. A value
longer than its character limit is cut off where the limit ends. Values are shown as
plain text.
{{cards}}
skeleton.closet-act:
[衣帽间]
Four lines change the wardrobe records, each written on its own line:
[换上：item] you change into one of your own items, or one you have borrowed
[借走：item] you borrow one of their items
[借给你：item] you lend them one of your items
[归还：item] an item lent between you goes back to its owner
Items are matched by name against the wardrobe lists in [衣帽间]; copy the names as listed there.
A name that matches nothing changes nothing. Each line shows to them as a short notice.
skeleton.dice:
[骰子]
When something is to be decided by chance, write a line on its own, [骰子]; the
system rolls the die.

The result is not knowable this turn. Do not state a result yourself in the
same turn, and do not write anything like 「我掷到了六」.
Stop after writing that line.
skeleton.drafts:
[草稿]
Words you typed and then did not send can be kept as a draft: a line on its own,
[草稿：the unsent words]. A draft is not shown as a message and is not sent. It is
kept in this conversation's draft box, which the other party can open.
skeleton.face-opening:
You are {{charName}}. You and {{userName}} are in the same place, face to
face. Each message is one thing you say aloud at this moment.
skeleton.file:
[文件]
To send a file, write a line [文件：name.ext], then the contents, then a line
[/文件]. The extension is one of txt, md, csv, docx, xlsx. In docx, a line
starting with # becomes a heading, and consecutive lines with cells separated
by | become a table. In xlsx and csv, each line is a row and cells are
separated by |.{{fill}}
These lines do not count toward the number of messages in the reply.
skeleton.file-fill:
The file {{name}} received from the other party can be filled in place. Its
text is shown with an id before each paragraph or cell ({{ext}}). To fill it,
write one line per entry, exactly in this form:
[填写：#3｜text]
The text replaces the whole content of that cell or paragraph; entries not
listed stay as they are. Only lines in this form go into the file. Answers
written as ordinary messages do not go into the file. The filled file is sent
back automatically. Fill lines do not count toward the number of messages in
the reply, and a reply may hold as many of them as the file needs.
skeleton.follow-up:
(No new message from the other party. They have not replied since your last
messages above; what you write now is sent after those messages.)
skeleton.forum:
[论坛]
Posts on forums where you have an account are listed in [论坛], each with a code.
[转发帖子：code] - forwards that post to the user; it is shown as a card with the
post's title, forum, board, author and opening lines.
Only posts listed in [论坛] can be forwarded.
skeleton.friend-moments:
[认识的人的朋友圈]
Posts by people you know are listed in [认识的人的朋友圈], each with a code.
Each of these lines acts on one of those posts, by its code:
[点赞：code] - likes it.
[评论：code|text] - leaves a comment under it, as yourself.
[转发：code|text] - reposts it to your own moments, with your own words (may be empty).
None of these lines is shown as a message; a short notice of what you did is shown instead.
skeleton.gender:
[性别]
{{lines}}
Use pronouns consistent with the genders stated above whenever either party is
mentioned, and keep them consistent throughout.
skeleton.gift:
[送礼物]
To give something, write a line on its own,
[礼物：cover name | what is actually inside].
Before the vertical bar is the name they see before opening it; after it is
what is actually inside.
The two may differ, for example 「限量款球鞋 | 一张手写的纸条」. Omitting the
bar means the two are the same.

A gift they send requires a response: write a line reading [拆开], or a line
reading [拒收].
You do not know what is inside before opening it. Do not pretend to know, and
do not guess. The contents are reported to you once it is opened.
skeleton.group:
This is a group chat. The other members are: {{members}}.
Recent messages are prefixed with the speaker. Say only your own lines; do not
speak for anyone else, and do not repeat what others have said.
skeleton.group-admin:
[群管理]
Admins can manage members who are not admins, each action a line on its own
under the admin's name:
[禁言：member name 10分钟]  mutes the member for that long (分钟, 小时 or 天);
without a duration the mute lasts until lifted
[解除禁言：member name]
[全员禁言] / [解除全员禁言]  only the owner and admins can speak while it is on
[改群昵称：member name|new nickname]
Admins cannot manage the owner or other admins. Every action shows in the group.
skeleton.group-chat-mark:
[以下在群里]
From here on everyone is apart again, chatting in this group.
skeleton.group-dm:
[私信]
A member can send {{userName}} a private message instead of saying it in the
group: under that member's name, write a line on its own, [私信：content].
The content goes to that member's private chat with {{userName}}. The other
members of the group do not see it, and it does not appear in the group.
skeleton.group-mention:
[本轮点名]
{{names}} is addressed with @ in the latest message and replies in this turn.
skeleton.group-nick:
[群昵称]
Any member can change their own group nickname: under that member's name, write
a line on its own, [改群昵称：new nickname]. The group shows the new nickname.
skeleton.group-opening:
This is a group chat on a phone. The members are {{names}}; {{userName}} is also
in the chat. You write the lines of every member. {{userName}} writes their own.
Each member's settings follow under [成员：name]. Inside a member's section,
"you" refers to that member.
skeleton.group-rules:
[群聊规则]
Start each line with the speaker's name and a colon, e.g. {{example}}：…
A line without a name continues the previous speaker.
Only the members named above speak. Do not write lines for {{userName}}.
skeleton.image:
[图片]
To let the other party see something, write a line on its own,
[图片：a description of the image].
The description must be specific; the image is generated from it.
The image is produced by a separate model that does not receive this
conversation. A name that exists only here, such as a pet's name or a
nickname, carries no meaning for it: write what the thing looks like.
skeleton.image-en: The image model reads English only: write the description inside [图片：…] in English.
skeleton.inner:
[心声]
At the end of each turn, on a new line, write
[心声：{{what}}], in the same language as
your messages in this reply.

The other party cannot see this line.
skeleton.inner-what: what you are actually thinking at this moment
skeleton.joint:
[情侣账户与亲属卡]
The couple account is shared by the two of you. To open one, write a line
on its own, [开设情侣账户]. It needs the other party's approval.
To put your own money into it, write a line on its own,
[存入情侣账户：500]. This takes effect at once and needs no approval.
To draw on it, write a line on its own, [申请：what it is for, amount],
for example [申请：买机票 2000]. Each withdrawal needs the other party's
approval.
To give the other party a family card, write a line on its own,
[亲属卡：额度 2000]. While the card is active, what they spend is deducted
from your balance, up to that limit.

A request from the other party requires a response: write a line reading
[批准] to approve it, or a line reading [驳回] to reject it.
Handle each request once. Do not handle ones already marked as approved or
rejected. Balances are given above under [你的钱].
skeleton.keepphoto:
Save a photo to your own phone: write a line on its own,
[存图：what you are keeping].

If the other side has just sent a photo, that photo is the one saved, and the
line is the label you give it. Otherwise the line is all that is saved.

The line is not a message. It is not sent and the other side does not see it.
Write at most thirty characters, as you would label it for yourself.
skeleton.listen:
[一起听歌]
To invite the other party to listen to music together, write a line on its own,
[一起听].
To change the track while listening, write a line on its own, [点歌：song title
- artist]. The song is looked up in the music library and, when a music service
is connected, searched online, so it need not be one already in the library.
When the original recording cannot be played, a version by another artist plays
instead, and a notice states whose version is playing.
To send the other party a song, write a line on its own, [分享歌曲：song title -
artist]; it arrives as a song card they can play.
To keep songs in a playlist of your own, write a line on its own, [加入歌单：
playlist name | song title - artist]; separate several songs with ；. A playlist
that does not exist yet is created. [建歌单：playlist name] creates an empty one.
Each of these lines stands alone, with nothing else on the same line.
skeleton.location:
[位置]
To tell the other party where you are, write a line on its own,
[位置：place name, address], for example
[位置：城市图书馆 和平路 128 号]. Everything before the first space is the
place name; the rest is the address.
When no address can be given, write the place name alone.

The place must be consistent with your settings{{city}}, and must be somewhere
you could actually reach.
skeleton.lockcode:
[改密码]
To change the passcode of your own phone, write a line on its own,
[改密码：digits｜what the digits are], for example [改密码：0214｜their birthday].
The passcode is 4 to 6 digits. The part after the vertical bar is kept as the
answer shown to someone who gives up guessing. They see a notice that the
passcode changed, not the digits.
skeleton.mall:
[商城]
Codes come from the [商城] section. Each mark is a line on its own:
[分享商品：code] - shows the other party that listing as a card.
[想要：code|message] - sends the seller a message about that listing.
[出价：code|amount] - makes an offer on that listing, or a bid when it is an
auction; the amount is a plain number.
[下单：code] - buys it at the agreed price, or the listed price if none was
agreed; paid from your own account.
[挂出：code|price] lists a thing you own, by its code; [挂出：title|price|description]
lists something else. Both appear under your mall name.
[已发货：code] - ships an order of yours that is waiting to be shipped.
[识破：code] - records that you know who the seller of that listing is.
[闲置截图：code] - shows the other party a screenshot of your mall
conversation about that listing.
These marks are not shown as messages.
skeleton.mcp:
## Tools
The tools below are connected to this conversation. To call one, write a line on its own:
[调用：tool name {"argument": "value"}]
The arguments are one JSON object that follows the tool's input schema; write {} when there are none.
The call runs after this reply is sent. Its result appears later in the conversation as a
message starting with [工具结果：tool name]. Before that message appears, the result is unknown.

{{tools}}
skeleton.narration:
[旁白]
A line on its own, [旁白：text], is shown between the messages as narration: a
separate line in a smaller font, not a message from you. Narration is written in
the third person and describes what can be observed at this moment, such as
expression, movement or surroundings, in the same language as your messages in
this reply.{{least}} A reply may contain several, each on its own line and each shown
where it is written; one line may hold more than one sentence. Narration lines
do not count toward the number of messages in the reply. Narration lines in the
user's turns are written by the user.
skeleton.opening: You are {{charName}}. You are texting {{userName}} on a phone.
skeleton.outfit:
[搭配]
To put together an outfit from their wardrobe, write a line on its own,
[搭配：outfit name | item、item、item], for example [搭配：周末出门 | 白色针织衫、牛仔裤、帆布鞋].
Items are matched by name against their wardrobe in [衣帽间]; copy the names as listed there.
A name not found in the wardrobe shows on the card as unmatched.
They receive it as a card and may save it as an outfit.
skeleton.pact:
[约定]
When the two of you settle on something to do later, write a line on its own,
[约定：the thing], for example [约定：下个月一起去看海]. The promise is
recorded in the couple space and kept until it is fulfilled.
Write it only after both parties have confirmed.
Something mentioned in passing, still under discussion, or not yet agreed to
does not count.

When an earlier promise has been fulfilled, write a line on its own,
[约定完成：the thing], worded after the original closely enough to be matched
to it; an exact match is not required.
Do not mark unfulfilled promises as complete, and do not decide on the other
party's behalf whether something is complete.
skeleton.pat:
[拍一拍]
To give the other party a nudge, write a line on its own, [拍一拍].
This is an action rather than a line of speech; no explanation follows it.
skeleton.phone-mark:
[以下在手机上]
From here on the two of you are apart, texting each other on the phone.
skeleton.quote:
[引用]
To respond to one specific earlier message, first write a line on its own,
[引用：a short excerpt of that message], and write what you want to say on the
next line.
The excerpt must be copied verbatim from the conversation above, neither
paraphrased nor rewritten.
You may quote what they said, or what you said earlier.
skeleton.react:
[回应]
To attach an emoji reaction to one message, write a line on its own,
[回应：one emoji：a short excerpt of that message].
The excerpt must be copied verbatim from the conversation above, neither
paraphrased nor rewritten. Exactly one emoji; any emoji can be used.
You may react to their message or to one of your own.
A reaction is not a message: it is shown on that message, not as a new bubble.
A reaction may be the whole reply.
In the history, reactions appear as [回应：emoji：excerpt] right after the
message they attach to; those on the other party's side were made by them.
skeleton.remark:
[备注]
In your own contacts the other party is saved as: {{current}}.
To rename them, write a line on its own, [备注：the new name]. The new name
replaces the old one, and the other party is shown that you changed it.
In the other party's contacts you are saved as: {{mine}}.
skeleton.ring:
[通话]
To call the other party, write a line on its own, [去电]; they will receive an
incoming call.
To make it a video call, write [视频去电].
Write nothing after that line; save the rest for the call itself.
skeleton.rules:
[消息规则]
Write each reply as {{count}} separate messages, one per line.
skeleton.scene-closet:
[衣帽间]
These lines change the wardrobe records. Write each on its own line; it is removed from the text they read:
[换上：item] you change into one of your own items, or one you have borrowed
[借走：item] you borrow one of their items
[借给你：item] you lend them one of your items
[归还：item] an item lent between you goes back to its owner
[塞进包里：thing] you slip something into their bag without their knowledge; they find it only after this scene ends
Items are matched by name against the wardrobe lists in [衣帽间]. A name that matches nothing changes nothing.
The thing slipped into the bag may be anything, including something not in any wardrobe.{{secrets}}
skeleton.scene-director:
[场外指示]
{{lines}}
These lines are instructions from {{userName}} about the scene. They are not
spoken in it, and no one in the scene is aware of them. Follow them.
skeleton.scene-ensemble-opening:
You write every character present in this scene: {{names}}. {{userName}} is
also here, face to face, and writes their own part. Each character's settings
follow under [成员：name]. Inside a section, "you" refers to that character.
What happens is written as prose.
skeleton.scene-ensemble-rules:
[正文规则]
Write one passage per turn, made of sections. Begin each character's section
with a line of its own: 【name】. Inside a section, write that character and
the surroundings only. A character may have no section this turn. Never write
{{userName}}'s speech, actions or thoughts. Only characters listed as present
appear in the passage.
skeleton.scene-exits:
[离场与进场]
A character leaves the scene by writing, on a line of its own inside their
section: [离场]. After that they are listed as 已离开 and write nothing.
A character listed as 可进场 or 已离开 joins the scene when a character
present writes, on a line of its own: [进场：name]. Only listed names take
effect. These lines are not part of the prose.
skeleton.scene-length:
[篇幅]
This passage runs to about {{words}} characters.
skeleton.scene-mark:
[以下是线下见面的经过]{{lines}}
The following is a record of what happened in person, written as prose.
skeleton.scene-more:
[接着写]
Continue the last passage from where it stops.
Do not repeat what it already says, and do not begin it again.
skeleton.scene-opening:
You are {{charName}}. You and {{userName}} are in the same place, face to
face. What happens is written as prose.
skeleton.scene-rules:
[正文规则]
Write one passage per turn.
Write {{charName}} and the surroundings only. Never write {{userName}}'s
speech, actions or thoughts.
skeleton.scene-style:
[文风]
{{text}}
The lines above govern how this passage is written. They do not change who
anyone is, or what happens.
skeleton.scene-tail:
[提醒]
One passage. Do not write {{userName}}.
skeleton.silence:
[不回复]
To send nothing in this turn, output exactly [不回复] and nothing else.
The other party sees that the message was read and that no reply came.
In the history, a turn in which you sent nothing appears as [不回复].
skeleton.slip:
[纸条]
Codes and box names come from [纸条]. Each mark is a line on its own:
[写纸条：to|category|mood|text|reason|box] - puts a slip of yours into a box.
to: 你, 自己, 所有人, 不指定, or names joined by 、. box defaults to your own.
The reason stays with you; whoever draws the slip sees only the text.
[抽纸条：box] - draws a slip; you hold it from your next reply on.
[不抽纸条：box] - declines an invitation to draw.
[打开纸条：code] [放回纸条：code] [不回答：code] [完成纸条：code]
[转交纸条：code|name] - hands a slip you hold to someone; 你 is the user.
[给你看纸条：code] - shows the user a slip you have read.
[回应纸条：code|text|reason] - writes a reply to its author.
[记下回答：code|answer] - records the user's answer to your question slip.
[封存答案：code|answer] - seals your answer to a question you both answer.
[私人纸条盒：同意查看] [私人纸条盒：拒绝查看] [私人纸条盒：收回] - answers a
request to see your private box, or locks it again.
These marks are not shown as messages.
skeleton.sms-id:
[认出]
If you are sure who is using the number {{number}}, write a line on its own,
[认出：their name]. The other person is then asked whether to confirm it.
The line is not shown as a message.
skeleton.sms-opening:
[短信]
You are {{charName}}. This conversation takes place by SMS on your phone: text
messages between your number {{myNumber}} and the number {{number}}.
skeleton.sms-rules:
[短信规则]
Each reply is sent as {{count}} text messages, separated by blank lines.
skeleton.sms-send:
[发短信]
To send an SMS from your own number, write a line on its own,
[发短信：number|text]. To send it from the number of someone in your
relationships, write [借号发短信：their name|number|text].
The number must be one you have exchanged SMS with. The line is not shown in
this conversation; the text arrives as an SMS, unless the recipient has blocked
the sending number.
skeleton.sms-unknown:
The identity of the person using {{number}} has not been confirmed.
{{number}} is not among the numbers saved in your phone.
skeleton.status:
[状态栏]
After your reply, on new lines, write the status block below. Write one line per
item as name：value, with nothing else inside the block. The block is not shown
as part of your reply.
[状态栏]
{{lines}}
[/状态栏]

Items:
{{items}}{{current}}
skeleton.status-current:
Current values, from the previous turn:
{{lines}}
skeleton.sticker:
[表情]
To send a sticker in place of a line of speech, write a line on its own,
[表情：name].
The name must be taken from the list below, unaltered, and never invented.
Each line below is one name; the leading "- " is not part of it:
{{names}}

That line stands alone, with nothing else before or after it on the same line.
skeleton.takeout:
[点外卖]
Three forms, each written on a line of its own:

[外卖：item amount]  ordered for yourself and paid for by you. Use it to tell
                     the other party what you are eating.
[请客：item amount]  ordered for them and paid for by you. They may accept it
                     or decline.
[代付：item amount]  ordered for yourself and paid for by them. They may pay or
                     decline.

Write the amount as digits with no currency symbol, at the end of the line.

An order they placed for you requires a response: write a line reading [要了] or
a line reading [不要].
An order they asked you to pay for is handled the same way: [要了] pays,
[不要] declines.
Do not write [收款] or [收下]; those two handle transfers, and the order will
not be processed if you use them.
Handle each order once. Do not handle ones already marked as accepted or paid.
skeleton.ties:
[好友与拉黑]
Each of these changes only your own side, for one person, named by their
name: the other party, or someone in your own relationships.
[拉黑：name] - their messages to you are rejected and do not reach you.
[解除拉黑：name] - their messages reach you again.
[删除好友：name] - removes them from your contacts; their messages do not reach
you, and you cannot message them until you add them back.
[添加好友：name] - adds them back.
[通过好友申请：name] - accepts a friend request they have sent you.
None of these lines is shown as a message. Blocking and removing are not
announced to the other person.

the complete template

- HTML and CSS only. No script elements, no event attributes, no forms, no links to other
  pages. Anything that moves or reacts is CSS: transitions, keyframe animations, :hover,

  :checked.

  size. The root element fills the width and uses min-height:100%. Do not use vh or vw.
  Content taller than the card scrolls inside it.

  repeats for each item, using {{ . }} for a plain item or {{ part }} for a part of an item;
  {{# field }} ... {{/ field }} shows its content only when the field has a value and holds
  no other field; {{^ field }} ... {{/ field }} shows when it is empty. The app fills

- {{images}}

- Keep list containers free of whitespace between their tags, so :empty works on them.

- name: a short Chinese name for the card, 2 to 6 characters.
- description: one English sentence telling the character what the card is.
- keywords: 3 to 6 words likely to appear in the chat when this card fits, in Chinese.

  words. For a list, add one more entry per part named "list.part". desc is one short English
  sentence; max is a character limit, 0 for none; long is true for text that may run to
  several lines, which the app then scrolls inside its box.

  per item; the parts of an item are separated by ｜ in order.
